Recipe: Snare (Level 1). You have seen a snare. A loop, a stick, an animal.

🪤 A man, maybe 40s, with a long braid catches you watching the snares come off the line. "...Want to actually SEE one?" They show you — the loop, the trigger stick, where the run narrows between the roots. "Opossum trails. Check at dawn. Always." Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
🚶 A woman, maybe 20s is back — found A person, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm.

Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.

— Open ground —
Grasshoppers rise in a clicking wave ahead of you. Something fork-tailed rides the wind above them, waiting for the careless ones.
Something moves out there — stripes flowing where no wind blows.
Something big is moving in the woods. The birds went quiet.
Movement — a crow watching you from a dead branch, head cocked.

This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.

Saplings push up through last year's deadfall, racing each other for the light. The forest never stops trying.
It followed you. The stripes flowing where no wind blows is here.
You see smoke on the horizon. Emberhold — 10 people, 3 days in. foragers, by the look of it. They know 3 plants — 3 new to you. They've been here the whole time.
Journal: Deep shade. The floor keeps its secrets.

Nobody at the fire knows your haul any better than you do. It'll be your own hands that teach you.
